Issued at 148 PM CDT Wed Oct 28 2026

This Afternoon and Tonight: Shower and Storm Details

Convective initiation has already taken place across west-
central Minnesota ahead of a shallow mid to upper tropospheric 
shortwave trough lifting northeastward through the Dakotas and 
Manitoba. Additional showers and storms will continue to develop
within this corridor of mid-level frontogenesis and theat-e 
advection, with cells likely growing upscale into clusters and 
lines in short order after initiation. Forecast soundings and 
hodographs over the Twin Cities still show the potential for 
embedded tornadoes with any organized lines or clusters, but 
given the narrow warm sector, the convective complex is expected
to start outrunning this instability axis by the time it 
reaches our forecast area after 22-00Z. 

The main wild card in the forecast revolves around how 
convection ahead this complex develops through the afternoon and
evening. There are hints in the explicit HRRR progs that more 
discrete cells develop over southern Minnesota and lift 
northeastward with time, which will have a better opportunity to
realize the limited instability (MLCAPE of 400-700 J/kg) but 
favorable lower tropospheric shear profiles and possibly 
produce a few weak tornadoes. The main area of concern for this 
is mainly along and west of a Rochester, MN to Wausau, WI line 
between 22-02Z.


Friday and Saturday: Trick or Treating Rain Possibilities

Broad subtropical high pressure lingers over the southeastern 
U.S. for Friday and Saturday, with return southerly flow working
northward along its western flank during this time. The theta-e
advection driven showers creep northward through the day on 
Friday, lifting through the rest of the forecast area Friday 
night into Saturday. However, with the upper level support 
waning during this time as the northern stream jet streak 
advances into Ontario, the showers should gradually lessen in 
intensity with the highest probabilities for 1/4-1/2 of an inch 
of rain (20-40%) staying over Iowa and lessening quickly as one
travels north. The slow-moving and decaying nature of the 
showers on Saturday makes it harder to pinpoint exactly what 
areas will be dry for Trick-or-Treating, so stay tuned for 
further updates as we get closer to Halloween.

Early Next Week: More Widespread Rain

A more dynamic weather setup evolves for the start of next week
as an energy exchange takes place between a pair of northern 
and southern stream waves over the Rockies, resulting in a rapid
deepening and closing off of the southern wave as it moves 
towards the TX/OK panhandles on Monday and Tuesday. The 
evolution and trajectory of the wave after this point becomes 
less certain as the medium range solutions quickly diverge. 
However, the main story for the local area--being on the 
northern side of the deformation zone/occlusion--will be a 
widespread period of rain starting from Monday evening 
potentially through Thursday. Overall rainfall amounts for the 
duration of the event could push over 1" (20-30% chance), but 
spread out over the course of several days with little in the 
way of impacts other than a span of several dreary days. The 
exact timing and location of this rain band will be fine tuned 
over the next few days.

Temperature Trends for the Week

Overall, after today's warmth, a cooler airmass arrives for the
rest of the week and into early next week. "Cooler" is a 
relative term with highs during this period still ranging from 
the upper 50s to upper 60s, still 5-10 degrees above average for
this time of year.
